annotation.title_clean: Clearview AI Inc v The Information Commissioner [2023] UKFTT 00819 (GRC)
annotation.title_en: Clearview AI Inc v The Information Commissioner [2023] UKFTT 00819 (GRC)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: First-tier Tribunal (General Regulatory Chamber), Information Rights
annotation.summary_en: UK First-tier Tribunal decision allowing Clearview AI's appeal against the ICO's enforcement and monetary penalty notices. It held that Clearview's facial-recognition scraping was related to behavioural monitoring under Article 3(2)(b) UK GDPR, but fell outside GDPR material scope because its clients are foreign law-enforcement and national-security bodies, so the ICO lacked jurisdiction.
key_provisions_or_claims: ICO lacked jurisdiction to issue the Enforcement Notice and Monetary Penalty Notice to Clearview.
Processing was related to clients' monitoring of UK data subjects' behaviour under Article 3(2)(b).
Article 3(2)(b) can apply where monitoring is done by a third party rather than the controller.
Clearview is joint controller with clients for search (Activity 2) processing.
Processing for foreign government law-enforcement and national-security functions is outside material scope (Art 2(2)(a) GDPR; Art 3(2A) UK GDPR).
